article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% indica / 30% sativa
Genetics: Northern Lights × Fast Buds Auto #1
Breeder: Fast Buds
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Less than 1%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Earth, pepper, spice, mild fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: Roughly 9 weeks from seed
Indoor Yield: Approximately 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Approximately 2–5 oz (50–150 g) per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Northern Lights Auto takes an old-school marijuana personality and places it inside a cultivation format designed for speed. Rather than reinventing Northern Lights with fashionable candy or dessert genetics, Fast Buds concentrated on characteristics that made the original family enduring: indica-heavy relaxation, sturdy growth, strong resin production and a distinctly earthy-spicy aroma.

Autoflower genetics change the plant’s schedule considerably. It does not wait for shortening daylight to begin blooming, can progress from seed to finished flowers in about nine weeks and remains manageable despite reaching a relatively substantial size for an auto. The result is cannabis that feels connected to an earlier era of weed breeding while offering the convenience expected from contemporary autoflowering seeds.
Genetics and Lineage

Fast Buds provides a more detailed lineage than the common description of Northern Lights crossed with generic ruderalis . Its published genetic tree places Northern Lights on one side and Fast Buds Auto #1 on the other. The Northern Lights branch traces back through Afghani and Thai material, while the autoflower side includes Lowryder #1, Northern Lights, Willy’s Wonder, ruderalis and Fast Bud Auto ancestry. Those components supplied the day-neutral flowering characteristic while allowing the breeder to retain much of the compact architecture and physical effect associated with classic Northern Lights.

This distinction becomes important because Northern Lights Auto is not one universally standardized cultivar. Numerous breeders have created automatic versions using different breeding stock, meaning THC , plant height, flowering time and aroma can differ significantly between seed companies. The specifications on this page refer specifically to the Fast Buds release rather than combining information from Royal Queen Seeds , Sensi Seeds , Green House Seeds or other Northern Lights autoflowers.
Effects and Experience

Physical relaxation establishes itself quickly. Fast Buds characterizes the onset as fast acting and strongly indica-like, with increasing consumption producing progressively heavier body effects. A moderate serving may begin with a noticeable release of muscular tension and a quieter mental tempo rather than an energetic cerebral rush. The experience tends to narrow the desire for activity as it develops, making movies, music, relaxing at home or preparing for sleep more compatible with the cultivar than tasks requiring sustained concentration.

Larger amounts push the experience much further toward couch-lock and drowsiness. The breeder specifically emphasizes heavy eyelids and full-body relaxation, so inexperienced consumers should not assume that an autoflower produces weaker cannabis simply because the plant matures faster. Current strain data places potency around 20% THC, but harvested flower can differ according to phenotype, lighting, environment and maturity. Cannabis can also slow reaction time, impair coordination and interfere with decision-making, making driving after consumption unsafe.
Medical Benefits

Among medical marijuana consumers, the appeal centers primarily on the cultivar’s deeply relaxing character. A patient already accustomed to THC-rich cannabis might consider a profile like this when seeking evening physical comfort, appetite support or help winding down before sleep. That does not mean Northern Lights Auto has been clinically demonstrated to treat insomnia, chronic pain, anxiety or another condition. Research on medical cannabis examines cannabinoids and standardized preparations; a breeder-specific strain grown under variable conditions cannot be assumed to provide a standardized therapeutic dose.

The less-than-1% CBD specification also indicates that this is not a balanced CBD cultivar. THC is therefore responsible for much of the psychoactive experience, which can become counterproductive at excessive doses. NIDA notes that THC-containing cannabis can alter mood, thinking and perception, and effects can vary substantially between individuals. Anyone managing significant symptoms, taking prescription medication or using marijuana as part of ongoing medical treatment should discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Northern Lights Auto belongs firmly to the savory side of the cannabis flavor spectrum. Fast Buds lists fruit, pepper and spice as its principal taste characteristics and describes the overall bouquet as more earthy than aggressively pungent. Breaking apart mature flower can reveal dry soil, cracked pepper and woody spice first, followed by enough soft fruit and sweetness to round out the sharper edges. The combination feels markedly different from the syrupy berry, cream and candy profiles prevalent in many newer hybrids.

Fast Buds does not currently provide a laboratory terpene analysis identifying individual compounds and percentages for this cultivar. For that reason, assigning a definitive myrcene, caryophyllene or pinene hierarchy would risk borrowing data from unrelated Northern Lights versions. The most accurate breeder-supported description is a savory terpene expression built around earth, pepper, spice and mild fruit, with the exact chemical profile dependent upon the harvested batch.
Growing Information

Speed is the defining cultivation advantage. Fast Buds gives Northern Lights Auto a nine-week cycle, with plants generally reaching 90–120 cm and yielding approximately 500–600 g/m² indoors or 2–5 ounces per plant outdoors. Since autoflowering begins according to plant age rather than seasonal photoperiod, there is no universal September or October outdoor harvest date. In favorable weather, growers instead calculate the approximate finish from germination. Fast Buds also highlights its ability to tolerate both cooler and hotter conditions, making the plant particularly appealing where outdoor seasons are short or unpredictable.

Its architecture retains recognizable indica characteristics . Short internodal spacing supports a compact canopy, while a thick central stem and substantial side branches carry resinous flowers. Fast Buds describes the buds as frosty and somewhat acorn-shaped, with swollen calyxes and abundant trichomes. The breeder also emphasizes resistance to pests and plant disease and recommends the strain for beginners.

Autoflowering simplicity still rewards careful management. Plants have limited time to recover from severe stress before flowering starts automatically, so overwatering, major root disturbance and unnecessarily aggressive training early in life can reduce final size. Steady growth during the first several weeks is particularly important because lost vegetative time cannot simply be regained by extending the light schedule before bloom.
FAQ
Is Northern Lights Auto indica or sativa?
Fast Buds classifies its version as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Its effect profile reflects that balance, leaning strongly toward physical relaxation, heaviness and eventual sedation.
What are the genetics of Northern Lights Auto?

Fast Buds traces the cultivar through Northern Lights and Fast Buds Auto #1. Its genetic tree shows Afghani and Thai ancestry behind Northern Lights, with Lowryder and ruderalis-related material contributing to the autoflowering branch.
How long does Northern Lights Auto take from seed to harvest?
Approximately nine weeks under good conditions. Fast Buds’ own cultivation guide also uses nine weeks from seed to harvest as its reference cycle, although environmental stress can delay development.
How much does Northern Lights Auto yield?
The breeder lists approximately 500–600 g/m² indoors and 2–5 ounces per plant outdoors. Final production depends on light, root development, nutrition, environment and plant health.
Is Northern Lights Auto easy to grow?

Yes. Fast Buds specifically positions this cultivar as beginner-friendly because of its low-maintenance structure, climate resilience and resistance to common pests and plant problems. Its automatic flowering also eliminates the need to switch to a 12/12 light schedule to trigger bloom.
Final Thoughts on Northern Lights Auto

Northern Lights Auto succeeds by modernizing a classic without burying its identity beneath newer flavor trends. The Fast Buds version preserves an indica-dominant experience, substantial resin development and a peppery, earthy, mildly fruity profile while adding automatic flowering and an exceptionally short cultivation cycle. A mature plant can reach 90–120 cm and produce surprisingly substantial harvests for an autoflower, yet its uncomplicated structure and environmental resilience keep it accessible to less experienced growers.

For consumers, this is primarily evening weed: physically relaxing, increasingly heavy with dose and much closer to traditional indica character than an energetic daytime hybrid. For cultivators, the combination of nine-week speed, strong branching, resin-covered flowers and broad climate tolerance explains its continued appeal. Because many breeders offer their own Northern Lights autos, keeping the breeder attached to the strain name is essential. In the case of Fast Buds, the cultivar represents a practical meeting point between classic Afghani-Thai cannabis ancestry and modern autoflower breeding.
